articleTitle: Stability of satellite communication networks with demand assignment multiple access
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The problem of stability is considered for satellite communication networks with demand assignment multiple access intended for voice communication and large data array transmission by means of FDMA or TDMA. The use of common channel signalling with random access of the "pure ALOHA" or "slotted ALOHA" type is assumed. For such networks the steady working conditions are shown to be different from from packet data transmission satellite networks using random access without the common channel signaling.

articleTitle: Inmarsat systems and services
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the current status and future development of mobile satellite communications services in the Inmarsat system. The evolution of user terminals from the original Inmarsat-A ship earth station for mariners to the global satellite paging system and hand held telephone for anyone on the move is a focal point of this discussion. The Inmarsat-A system and the variety of its applications and services continue to be Inmarsat's prime revenue generator. The growing family of new Inmarsat systems and services are increasingly contributing to the expanding markets, traffic and revenues for mobile satellite services around the world. This include Inmarsat-C, a data messaging system using small, portable terminals and Inmarsat's aeronautical satellite communications system as well as the newest additions-Inmarsat-M, which brings to the world a low-cost, portable satellite phone service and Inmarsat-B, a digital successor to Inmarsat-A.

articleTitle: Combined signal processing in satellite communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: A class of adaptive combined systems for spreaded-band signal processing in satellite telecommunication systems is described. Expressions for the optimal weight factors which allow the processing performance to be assessed on the background of spreaded-band and narrow-band interference are generated. The analysis of combined processing features is close to the Wiener-Hopf solution, particularly, the principal recurrence of providing an optimal solution is shown.

articleTitle: Modern small satellites projects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The advantages of using small satellites in space scientific and technological activity are discussed. These relatively cheap satellites are characterized by a mass from one kilogram up to several hundred kilograms, dimensions under 1 meter and a relatively simple set of scientific and auxiliary equipment. They can be orbited as a piggy-back with a main satellite, by a low-power launcher, or by a multiple-launch spacecraft. The small satellite projects under development throughout the world are considered. Special attention is given to Russian projects and their launching possibilities. The most commonly used attitude control systems (ACS) for small satellites are highlighted. A majority of Russian small satellites are equipped with a gravity gradient ACS. The ACS of the universal small space platform, a typical small satellite with mass of about 60 kg, is discussed in detail. The platform is being developed as a universal commercial satellite.

articleTitle: Improvement of the navigational position determination stability through the navigation system memory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: A new approach to improve the accuracy and stability of space navigation/time determination is proposed and investigated. The covariance between the components' estimation error covariance matrices (user coordinates and timing addition) changes with the change of geometry factor. This may be used for improvement of the navigational position determination stability.

articleTitle: The role of VSATs and other small satellite terminals in the evolving telecommunications environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Small terminals with dishes ranging from less than 1 m to 2.4 m are commonly used in international satellite systems such as EUTELSAT. Typical applications are: TVROs (TV receive only) for direct TV reception from satellites, SNG (satellite news gathering) with lightweight flyaway antennas, and VSATs (very small aperture terminals) for data distribution or transaction processing networks. The increasing importance of VSAT and other small satellite terminals has been recognized by the ITU, which has carried out extensive studies on these issues and related matters within the ITU-R Sector for the radio aspects and the ITU-T Sector for network and standardization related aspects. The paper discusses the general key aspects including a summary review of the ITU work, and points out some differences which exist between European countries in the perception of the concept of VSAT. It also addresses the use of VSAT and other small terminals in the EUTELSAT system, with particular attention to the provision of services to the many eastern European countries which have become members of the Organization.

articleTitle: Dubna-Intercosmos International Experimental Satellite Communications Centre
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The International Experimental Satellite Communications Centre was established to handle satellite communication and television broadcasting problems. The paper discusses various technical facilities used at the Centre. They include earth stations of different types and services, terrestrial test links, radiometers and a computer centre. The paper considers research results in the following areas: developing higher frequency ranges (above 10 GHz) and applications of digital TV and data transfer techniques and installations. It also outlines a few projects based on a commercial use of satellite communication and broadcasting systems at 14/11 GHz.

articleTitle: Ku-band power amplifier MIC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The results of the design and fabrication of a Ku-band power amplifier MIC are presented. The frequency range of the MIC is from 14.0 GHz to 14.5 GHz. The key elements of the MIC with an output power of up to 250 mW are GaAs FETs.

articleTitle: Low noise converter for Ka-band communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: A low noise converter has been designed and fabricated for Ka-band communication systems. The components of low noise converter are the LNA and the balance mixer. The converter has following parameters: the noise figure is less than 6.0 dB, the input frequency range is from 36 to 38 GHz, the output frequency is 1.2 GHz and and the conversion gain is 15 dB. The key element of the LNA is the GaAs FET.

articleTitle: Intersatellite optical communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Presents the results of research designed to create a new type of communications, intersatellite optical communication lines (IOCL). In space the propagation media is a vacuum, so it is possible to use the optical band for intersatellite information transmission. The very short wavelength allows one to obtain ultra-narrow light beams (several angle seconds) and to support high speed duplex information transmission at huge distances (<100000 km) with a level of high security.

articleTitle: Digital compression of TV images for the transmission through the satellite channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The results of computer simulations of compression algorithms for digital TV images, providing the possibility of transmitting several TV programs in a single satellite channel are presented. The enhancement of the interframe compression efficiency is achieved due to the adaptive variation of the coefficient of transmission precision based on the assessment of the specific features of the image being processed and the splitting of the image into separately processed and coded constituents. The modified algorithms for luminance and chrominance signals processing were developed to ensure the transmission of 4-6 TV programs in a single standard radio channel without visible distortions.

articleTitle: Low Earth orbit satellite communication system Courier 1
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The low orbit global satellite system (GSS) for data exchange and communication Courier-1 is being designed and manufactured by a group of electronics companies within the ELAS Scientific and Research Company and a group of rocket-space companies headed by the COMPLM Scientific and Technological Company. The GSS is based upon a low Earth orbit satellite system network and is intended to provide low cost, reliable and high quality data communication services to anywhere from anywhere in the world at any time through small users terminals including portable terminals. GSS is based on the onboard and terrestrial equipment that has been developed by ELAS. The satellite group is to be deployed and supported through the START multipurpose transportable space launch system with the solid propellant launch vehicle based on the SS-25 ICBM. The report gives an idea of the general structure of the Courier-1 system and provides an overview of relations between different its units.

articleTitle: On new approaches to complex interactive TV system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: It is shown that due to the development of digital multiprogramme TV broadcasting and a substantial increase of data traffic, TV viewers are receiving a large amount of information. For the effective usage of this information viewer responses and transmission of corresponding messages are necessary. The interest of information sources in return channels is pointed out. The importance of the study is related to the construction of new interactive TV systems having hundreds of thousands of return narrow-band digital channels connecting TV viewers and TV data users with sources of information. It is reported that up to now the tendency to use cable TV and telephony for these purposes has dominated. A new complex approach to interactive TV systems construction, taking into account the potentialities of cable TV, telephone networks, cellular networks, low orbital satellite systems, etc., is proposed. The possibility of using receiving antennas as transmitting ones while providing TV viewers with low power digital radio transmitters as elements of TV sets and mobile radio tranceivers is also stressed. The importance of interactive TV systems construction in regions with low population density in order to provide TV viewers with additional services, is pointed out.

articleTitle: Small satellite communications station
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The small satellite communications station is designed for operation in the communications systems where signal processing is used to increase the interference immunity and in multiple access systems with code or code-time signal sharing. The station can be used in digital information transmission and exchange systems. The main principles used in the construction of such stations are outlined.

articleTitle: System of space optico-electronic complexes and their ground-based support
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Discusses the characteristics and uses of remote sensing equipment onboard satellites. In particular the authors consider: SERNA-NH for the space system ARKON, 2. SPLAV-ECO for the space system RESURS-SPEKTR, 3. SELVA for the space system ALMAZ-1V, and 4. KOE-03 for the space system OBZOR.

articleTitle: On the problem of coordination of architectural decision for satellite system for remote sensing of the Earth and automated ecological monitoring with appropriate geophysical and ecological models
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Firstly, models of satellite systems for remote sensing of the Earth and automated ecological monitoring are considered. Secondly, appropriate geophysical and ecological models are discussed. The possibility for assessment of architectural decisions for systems of a particular class is shown in the framework of the SLAMSYSTEM simulation modelling environment.

articleTitle: Ka-band low noise amplifier
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: A three stage low noise HEMT amplifier has been designed and fabricated for Ka-band applications. The key element of the low noise amplifier is an AlGaAs-GaAs HEMT with a 0.3 /spl mu/m gate length and a gate width of 60 /spl mu/m, that was designed and manufactured in SRI "Pulsar" technology. The HEMT has shown a minimum noise figure of 1.7 dB and an associated gain of 4.0 dB at 37 GHz. The three-stage amplifier has demonstrated a gain of 16 dB and a low noise figure of 2.8 dB at 37 GHz, the input and output return losses are better then -21 dB and -23 dB respectively.

articleTitle: Inmarsat-P the world in your hand
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The hand-held satellite telephone Inmarsat-P will fulfil one of mankind's ultimate dreams, the ability to communicate instantly and conveniently virtually anywhere on Earth. Inmarsat, a world leader in global mobile satellite communications, is well advanced in its planning for this global mobile phone of the future, with introduction targeted for 1999-2000. An overview is given of Inmarsat's approach to the challenge of developing and implementing this global hand-held phone service.

articleTitle: Improvement trends of the space observation systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Discusses various means by which remote sensing observations may be improved. In particular the authors consider: information output increase, information semantic value increase, radiometric and photogrammetric property provision, setting up a means of information efficient delivery for the mass consumer.

articleTitle: AmRussCom-digital communications in Russia
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: AmRussCom is the leader in satellite communications systems serving the oil and gas industry in Russia with voice and data communications. AmRussCom provides hub station services in Moscow from several teleport facilities. AmRussCom operates a backbone microwave link that connects several teleport facilities. Other offerings include providing telecommunications services, system rentals, network engineering and management.

articleTitle: Satellite telecommunication in technical university
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Discusses the use satellite telecommunication systems at Moscow Technical University to train young engineers. The educational experimental centre for satellite reception and transmission is used for studying radio engineering and space systems and for laboratory work.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional satellite antenna supplying rejection in direction needed
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic compatibility is one of importance in the VHF-SHF band LEO system design. One of the approaches to resolve this problem is employment of antenna adaptive control methods. But in the case of a simple omnidirectional antenna these methods are useless, as they are based on multielement antennas. The proposed approach to resolve this problem is based on choosing the geometry of the antenna to form a null level of directivity according to the known supply current distribution. An omnidirectional antenna design for satellite terminal use is discussed. It consists of orthogonal crossed dipoles (each in x, y, z axis) possessing a common center. That system of three dipoles is able to form a null level of directivity according to their size ratio and power supply.

articleTitle: First computer prediction of radiated fields of modern antennas for Earth and air/space communication systems and radars
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: A novel universal model for wide class of reflector or hybrid antennas with second-order curve profiles and any possible mirror edge form is presented. Both symmetrical and offset geometry is available. For hybrid antennas their feed array may have up to a few hundred independently placed and excited elements. The constructed model has been realized in two program packages: AntMaster and FARFOR for IBM-compatible personal computers. The model provides more than just a reduction in the computation effort, so that users of the program packages can easily analyze and synthesize multielement arrays, reflector and hybrid antennas practically in a real-time mode.

articleTitle: Versions of the low Earth orbit satellite communication systems design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The different variants of system structure and parameter choice depending on system requests are considered in the article. On the basis of selected groups, which consist of 24 or 36 spacecraft with a symmetrical structure and orbit altitude 1600 km, it is demonstrated that one can have a high communication provision probability (0.98...1.0) in regional and regional-global communication systems. Such systems cover entire continents, where the connectivity is provided only by restricted Earth transponders, and in global systems-by a communication provision combined method, i.e. by usage of intersatellite communication links for two directions in each spacecraft and some Earth transponders.

articleTitle: The role of satellite communication in network reliability improvement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: One of the essential aspects of application of the satellite communication in Russia is connected with the improvement of the reliability of present communication systems. A program for creating a satellite telecommunication system for the gas industry of Russia (system "Yamal") is being developed by JSC GAZCOM. The satellite system will be especially useful for the important gas production centres of the North-Tumen region in West Siberia, where terrestrial communications are not fully developed. This paper presents the results of a comparison of the reliability of the existing communication network and the future network using satellite communications. An original application program package was used for the calculations. The results obtained show that using satellite communication allows a reduction of the unavailability by more than tenfold.

articleTitle: "Globsat" low-orbit communication system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Much attention is being given to the development of low orbit communications systems. An analysis of the available materials shows the following. The majority of the proposed systems are devised to operate with a large number of spacecraft (from 36 to 66). In most cases, rather complex apparatus, which incorporate a control system, propulsion plant, command radio link and intersatellite communications facilities, are used as the communication spacecraft.

articleTitle: Data transmission space system for air traffic control in Russia
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The Federal Program of Modernisation of Universal Air Traffic Control System of Russia provides use of space facilities for navigation, tracking and communications. To fulfil this provision of the program, the data transmission space system for air traffic control has been developed. This system is designed to provide automatic air traffic control system operation in Russia. It performs the following tasks: global navigation support of planes under accuracy of coordinates definition better than 100 meters; precise navigation support in airport areas; communications services between regional air traffic control centers and aeroplanes (mobile telecommunications); automatic dependent tracking of aeroplane flights; and voice and data communications between components of the air traffic control system. The Federal Program is based on the deployment of satellite systems.

articleTitle: TV signals effective coding for the satellite videoconferencing systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: For satellite videoconferencing systems the problems of reducing the transmission speed to the values corresponding the CCIR Recommendations H.120 and H.130 on the basis of pyramid coding and vector quantization (VQ) coding methods and their combination with other effective TV signals coding methods are presented. Some methods of nonorthogonal (Laplacian pyramid) and orthogonal pyramid coding are investigated.

articleTitle: Low availability system design for satellite communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The effects of propagation anomalies on some of the parameters are considered and some results of extensive attenuation measurements are given. As an example, a Ka-band VSAT system that exploits suitable impairment countermeasure is shown. The performance of the proposed communication system is evaluated using the experimental data and a comparison with the results obtained using ITU-R prediction methods is presented, as well.

articleTitle: Acoustooptics possibilities for increasing operation efficiency of low-earth orbit satellite on-board adaptive arrays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The possibilities of acousto-optic processor applications for increasing low-earth orbit satellite on-board adaptive array operation efficiency is shown. A classification of adaptive arrays realizing optical methods of signal processing is proposed. The technical possibilities of modern acoustic-optic processors are analyzed and conclusions concerning the addition to low earth orbit satellite on-board adaptive arrays of multichannel acousto-optic spectrum analyzers is made. Block-diagrams of on-board adaptive arrays with multichannel acousto-optic spectrum analyzers are elaborated.

articleTitle: Design of a rapidly acquiring and noise immune PLL for communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Phase-locked loops (PLLs) are extensively used for carrier synchronization. For signals with slowly varying phase and frequency, the best performance is achieved with PLLs. However, PLLs cannot provide rapid acquisition with high probability when acquiring signals with high a priori phase and frequency uncertainty because of the hang-up phenomenon. This paper presents a new approach to the synthesis of PLLs employing the indirect nonlinear filtering theory. Through Monte Carlo simulations, the use of this approach is shown to allow the creation of a PLL devoid of the hang-up phenomenon. It also provides a wider pull-in range, more rapid acquisition without degrading the estimation accuracy in the tracking mode, and a lower probability of losing lock than the traditional algorithms of the PLL do.

articleTitle: Data compression in the digital TV
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The article examines the problem of video data compression as a means of telecommunication networks optimisation. The main practical problem is the point-to-point conformity of the restored and original images. The methods used to solve this problem can be divided into two groups. One group is based on integrated conversions (discrete cosine transform, Walsh transform, etc.) and the other group enables data compression without integrated conversions. Video signal compression in the first group is accompanied inevitably by quantization, and threshold processing of its components. Within the second group we consider an adaptive sampling-local differential coding video data compression method for use in digital TV systems.

articleTitle: MicroSputniks of packet radio to 4 kgs the warranty of decrease of costs in 20 time
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The basis of the Sputnik packet radio network is the space repeater. The temperature control system of the space repeater uses a heat-conducting lattice which levels the temperature difference between sunlit and shadow areas. The packet radio functions all levels (physical, channel, network, transport, session, representative, application) of the ISO OSI model with gateways into telephone networks, X25, Ethernet and ARCNET networks.

articleTitle: Development concept of the multipurpose system of the low orbital small size of satellites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Describes the development of low orbital systems of small size satellites. Studies of the general design of monitoring spacecraft aimed at monitoring ground and space situations on a regional and planetary scale are presented. The spacecraft are built on the basis of small satellites which can be placed into orbit by converted rocket launchers. The satellites provide spectral zonal images of the Earth's surface with different spatial resolutions. The satellites are equipped with a servo platform on which the payload apparatus (viewing TV camera, low and high resolution telescopes, thermovisor) is located. The basic requirements for satellites' orbital placement and for technical equipment are determined.

articleTitle: "Express" satellite communications system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The "Express" satellite communications system which will be a fundamental part of Russian satellite communication is described.

articleTitle: SATELLITE COMMUNICATIONS IN RUSSIA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94

articleTitle: Routing according to the required time of route existence criteria for low Earth orbit satellite networks with the dynamically variable topology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Routing according to the criterion of the required time of route existence is a task of importance in the field of information interchange in satellite data networks. The designed procedure provides the construction of a quasi-optimal route that is continuous during a previously defined time interval. The designed algorithms and program have been used for obtaining some specific characteristics of the routes which have predetermined existence times.

articleTitle: On construction of global satellite multiprogram high definition television and high quality sound broadcasting system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Big screen high quality television is available by using broadband high definition television (B-HDTV) systems. Construction of the multiprogram direct satellite B-HDTV broadcasting system and direct high quality sound broadcasting system is a fundamental scientific and technical problem being of interest to both international cooperation and foreign investments attraction. Construction of a multiprogram direct high definition broadcasting system and high quality sound broadcasting may interest almost all those countries which manufacture TV sets, digital personal radio receivers as well as big sound broadcasting, television broadcasting, and film companies, and those European, American, and Japanese companies which design and develop satellite transponders and earth stations. Foreign partners may be incorporated in the system as investors and owners, users (leaseholders), and participants of the project for the implementation of the space and earth segments.

articleTitle: Communication satellite unified buses perspectives and capabilities
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Discusses the MSS-2500-GSO-01, MSS-2500-GSO-02, and MSS-2500-GSO satellite buses for the Russian communication satellite market. In particular the authors mention bus performances and resources set up.

articleTitle: Outlooks for development of mobile satellite communication in Russia
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The main trends in the development of mobile space communication in Russia are reflected in the article. The basic performance characteristics of the Russian satellites being developed and the organization of mobile space communication in Russia are examined. Taking into account the geographical position of the country it is necessary to use geostationary, high-elliptical and low Earth orbits for creating the mobile satellite service.

articleTitle: Characteristic investigation of availability of surface and cosmic abonents in satellite information network on the basis of low-orbit artificial Earth satellites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Discusses the results of a study of constructing a satellite information network (SIN) with the use of a network satellite-retranslator (SR). A simulation model was worked out to investigate the orbital configuration of artificial Earth satellite-retranslators, consisting of several artificial Earth satellites.

articleTitle: Information satellite systems for the financial industry organizations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Summary form only given. Both the existing and new satellite communications segments are used in the proposed program of the information satellite system establishment for the financial industry organizations. Space segment development is oriented to capacity increase, multi-access, and supports both VSAT networks and main wideband channels. The ground switching system is based on special radiocommunication, radiorelay and optical-fiber communications lines and locking elements, and is development for switching computers and local computer networks. Geostationary satellites and low-earth orbit satellite systems are introduced into the data system combinations. These systems are: Potok-1 (GEO), Kupon (GEO), Courier (LEO). At the present time the work to integrate the indicated systems with each other and with other systems for providing the possibility of interconnecting users of these systems is being carried out.

articleTitle: Precision gyromoment attitude control systems of rapid manoeuvring spacecrafts for remote sensing and land-survey
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Presents results for precision gyromoment attitude control systems (ACSs) for fast-manoeuvring low-orbital remote sensing spacecraft (RSS) with a moment gyrocomplex (MGC) in the form of a minimum-excessive scheme of four gyrodines (GDs) with electromagnetic suspension (EMS) of the rotors. The authors discuss the employment of mathematical models, methods, algorithms and software for their optimization and dynamic investigation.

articleTitle: Satellite communications system using VSAT's and POTOK satellite-transponder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: System "SOKOL-0" can be considered as computer network VSAT's connected by satellite communication channels with a master computer at the central ground station. The important feature of the system consists in information receiving/transmission automation: taking into account priorities of uses and messages and connection provision, information exchange, mail handling, book keeping, and some other operations which don't require operator interference. The channel protocol provides automated error correction using antinoise coding and automated retransmission of information with uncorrected errors. The system space segment consists of "POTOK" satellite-transponders.

articleTitle: Satellite communication systems in radio amateur frequency band "Radio-M"
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Discusses the project of a low-orbit system of satellite communication-"Radio-M" in the radio amateur frequency band. The deployment of the space segment of this system is proposed to be carried out by means of the launch vehicle "Rokot" with the "Briz" upper stage.

articleTitle: "BANKIR" satellite communication system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The "BANKIR" satellite network is a communication and information network integrating the latest Russian technologies for operation of clearing and data processing systems for financial, banking and other commercial operations. In addition to banking communication the "BANKIR" network will provide various types of long distance and regional telecommunications, TV/radio broadcasting, teleconferencing and business communication. The "BANKIR" satellite network is based on "KUPON" series satellites and will include three satellites which could provide coverage of most of the Earth's surface. The system is designed to serve Russia and CIS, but the spare capacity of the satellites transponders may be utilised anywhere in the serviceable area.

articleTitle: Advanced microstrip networks for integrated mobile communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The increasing demand for mobile communications calls for the development of advanced components to reduce the size and the cost and improve the performance of transceivers. This paper presents high performance multiport hybrid networks and specific components in thick film microstrip for phased-array antennas at 1.6 (satellite mobile equipments) or 1.8 GHz (DCS 1800). For the sake of brevity, in what follows only the case of DCS 1800 is discussed.

articleTitle: LOCSS-system for Earth monitoring with the direct access to space information
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Since the 70's remote sensing space-based systems have developed by means of the continuous increase of the resolution of the Earth observation instruments, of the number of spectral channels and the swath width. This has resulted in the enlarging of the amount of data obtained by the onboard instrumentation together with the data transmission capacity of the communications channels. As a consequence, data reception from the main space systems which observe the Earth from space (Landsat, SPOT, "Resurs-O") can only be carried out by special receiving stations equipped with sophisticated, and, sometimes, unique devices. In the present situation it is necessary to search for simple and effective technological solutions capable of eliminating the contradictions between the methods of data acquisition and data processing and of reducing the distance between the source of information and the real user. The organization of spaceborne data reception directly by users themselves could be such a solution. The authors consider such a system and the configuration of its onboard instrumentation from the user's point of view.

articleTitle: Airborne relay complex of the 14/11 GHz band fixed satellite system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The airborne relay complex (ARC) was designed by NPO "SPURT" at NPO "ELAS" to work in the satellite communication system "BANKIR" within the geostationary satellite transponder (ST) "KUPON". In the first instance, the ARC was designed in order to provide satellite communication for the Russian Federation Central Bank. However, the principles on which the ARC design is based, make it possible to set up multifunctional communication networks for various organizations, departments and companies. The main specifications of the ARC are given. The ARC represents a 24-channel 14/11 GHz band transponder with direct signal retransmission. By frequency band reuse, 24 channels with a 36 MHz bandwidth are realized.

articleTitle: The controlled flat-layered medium as a basis for new methods and airborne communication devices development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: We offer a new method of radio telecommunication, in which the information signal is formed and extracted by reflecting artificial discontinuities, represented by controlled flat-layered mediums. We also state the fundamentals of such mediums synthesis theory, describe their functionality, experimental results and their analysis.

articleTitle: Combined satellite communications systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The article describes the possibility of decreasing the load on geostationary orbits through the creation of combined satellite telephone communications systems using space vehicles located both on geostationary and low Earth orbits. Estimations of the capacity of the systems and the gain such systems will provide are made.

articleTitle: Overview and design of the Glonass system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Discusses the history of the Glonass system, including: the satellite subsystem, monitoring and control subsystem, navigation field monitoring, user equipment, experimental system data, international applications and system prospects.

articleTitle: The monitoring system based on date spaceborn photos territory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Abnormal optical contrast in spaceborn photos is used as a criterion for the purity of the atmospheric layer near the Earth. Software is created for the analysis of the spaceborn video information. The possibility of the creation of software for the purity control of the atmosphere is discussed, air-space monitoring of an industrial city being taken as an example.

articleTitle: Unified transceivers "Oktant" in 4/6 and 11/14 GHz range for small communication-satellite earth stations and data-sending stations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: A special feature of the production of transceiving equipment of communication satellite earth stations is the relatively small number of fully developed products available. The transceivers are used in two frequency ranges, 4/6 and 11/14 GHz. They differ in composition depending on the purpose (terminal or central), functions (digital data transmission or telephony), siting (stationary or mobile). Production profitability in this case depends much on the extent of the samples uniformity. The paper presents the development results of transceivers for earth stations, the main feature of which is the unification of circuitry, and the design and technological approaches, which makes it possible to meet most of the consumers' requirements with the minimum of expense.

articleTitle: The new satellite communication system for Russia "Yamal"
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The new satellite communication system "Yamal" based on geostationary satellites is created by the joint-stock company GAZCOM for the gas industry and other customers. The paper presents the main characteristics of this satellite communication system including the transponder characteristics, the parameters of the earth stations, the structure of control system and the types of networks created.

articleTitle: Development concept of the ecomonitoring, using small satellites and ground station network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Summary form only given. Discusses a satellite system for remote sensing. The authors briefly describe features of the satellite and its equipment together with its communication link with the ground and the transmission of information.

articleTitle: Algorithms of measuring the angular coordinates of objects with an unknown baseline on the basis of global satellite navigation systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Global satellite navigation systems intended for high precision measurement of coordinates, velocities and time have been widely developed. The study of equipment functional possibilities for users of these systems is of great interest. Of particular importance is the study of possibilities to measure, on the basis of global satellite navigation systems, an object's angular coordinates with a high accuracy, for example, space vehicles where it is of vital importance to know the base angular position in relation to both a precision antenna pointing to the Earth and orientation of solar cells and sidereal transducers. When measuring the angular coordinates the following cases are discussed: measurement of the angular coordinate position of the baseline-vector lying in a horizontal plane; measurement of the baseline-vector space angular position; measurement of object space angular position. The task of angular coordinate measurement may be complicated if the baseline-vector is a priori unknown.

articleTitle: Communication satellites: orbital information efficiency
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The dependence of the relative daily average amount of information transmitted on the altitude and inclination of the spacecraft's circular orbit are obtained. The notions of the integral density of the information flow available at the earth station visibility zone and the integral density of the daily global information flow are introduced as the orbital efficiency indices. The specific expense per information unit depending on the orbit altitude is also estimated.

articleTitle: "Condor"-satellite communication system with mobile objects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The article deals with a satellite communication system project which incorporates geostationary orbit satellites. A comparison is included of analogous foreign and home systems. The main aim is to help the interested parties to clarify the main technical and economic aspects of the conception of the "Condor" communication system.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of Osman Nuri Ucan (ONU)-receiver for trellis coded M-QAM schemes in partial response channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Trellis coded M-QAM modulated signals are analysed in a partial response channel using the Osman Nuri Ucan (ONU)-receiver proposed by Ucan in 1992. The ONU-receiver is composed of k-parallel unit memory decoder, k/k+1 rated systematic encoder, cascaded with a PRS channel model. The combined trellis structure of ONU-receiver reduces the state number from 2/sup k/2/sup /spl nu//2/sup k+1/ resulting from k-unit memory of the parallel precoders, /spl nu/ unit memory of the systematic encoder and (k+1) unit memory of the PRS channel model to only 2/sup k+/spl nu//. Therefore considering the PRS channel together with classical trellis coded M-QAM structures does not increase the state number and decoding complexity. The ONU receiver improves both the bandwidth efficiency and error performance with no resulting increase in the decoding complexity. As an example, the error event lower bound of the ONU-receiver is derived for 4QAM-TCM having an encoder memory /spl nu/=1 and /spl nu/=2 in AWGN and colored noise environments.

articleTitle: Satellite communication systems with the use of long-duration satellites intended for operation in highly-elliptical orbit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The authors discuss the development of the Mayak satellite for communications. Coverage aspects and orbits are discussed in particular.

articleTitle: On antenna feed system for the microwave satellite communications earth station
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The report shows the advantages of using phased antenna systems for long distance satellite communication. It also shows the structure and the working principles of a device for accurate phasing of antennas with high space diversity, which are connected to the receiver by microwave feeder lines. The author suggests the control signal structure and an algorithm of its use for highly accurate measurement of the electric length of very long microwave feeder lines. Also considered are specifications of the phased antenna and its advantages over large single antennas.

articleTitle: ELECON-STIR multi-purpose satellite system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The ELECON-STIR multipurpose satellite system is developed to solve the following tasks: to track mobile transport vehicles, including maritime vessels; to monitor a consignment integrity; and to provide telecommunications services. To control a transport vehicle by the ELECON-STIR system, an automatic radio beacon with autonomous power supply is installed. On-ground stations of the Regional Control Center defines the plane coordinates of the transport vehicle using data acquired from the radio beacon through the satellite. These data in connection with the timing scale and container's identification (ID) are transmitted to the Traffic Control Center (TCC). Data transmitted to the TCC are organised and distributed to the appropriate sectors and directions. To check the container integrity, a radio beacon and container integrity registration sensors are installed in the container. The main customers of the system are railroad companies, truck companies and maritime companies.

articleTitle: Satellite communications links' energy capacities required to provide interference immunity receiving of phase shift keyed signals in case of non-linear transponder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The performance of satellite communications links with digital signals operating through a transponder with a non-linear input-output power and phase-input power relationships is considered. It is possible to simplify the calculations of the effects of the link signals interaction in their passage through the transponder if the pair of weight functions of the non-linear input-output power and phase-input power relationships are used for interpolation of the non-linearity. Taking into account that the signals at the input of the earth station decisive units are represented in the form of the sum of components with known probability density functions and changing the order of the averaging over the random signals' parameters in calculating the error probability, the estimations of the signal probability density function characteristics at the decisive unit input are obtained. The relationship of one binary symbol error versus transmitting signal power in this link when the power of the other links is also determined.

articleTitle: Satellite personal communication system "SPS-SPUTNIK"
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The State Rocket Centre "Academician V.P. Makeyev Design Bureau" is developing the "SPS-SPUTNIK" satellite personal communication system. The article throws light on the system's features and its position among the satellite communication systems, the system's structure and capabilities, orbital structure of the space segment and ground components, setting-up of a radio channel and facilities for system deployment based on converted serial missiles and the independent ground launching complex.

articleTitle: Global satellite backbone network for interconnections between high speed LANs, MANs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The principles of interconnecting existing high speed LANs and MANs are discussed. The interconnections are done by means of a geostationary space ring network (SRN), comprising 12 Advanced Technology Communications Satellites, equipped with multibeam antennas and providing intersatellite connectivity and onboard demodulation and information processing. The space ring network performs the tasks of the backbone network and actually is the highest layer of a hierarchic multilayer high speed computer network. The lowest layers of this network are existing LANs and MANs. The network interconnections are based upon so-called Z-BRIDGEs. These bridges provide internetwork retransmission of frames, the routing function being performed by special hardware. The Z-BRIDGEs provide secure transparent connections between any computers belonging to different networks, either public switched or private, at any site world-wide.

articleTitle: Efficiency enhancement of the space low-orbit system GONETS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The Scientific Production Institute for Applied Mechanics (NPO PM) is developing the GONETS low-orbit space communication system. The system exploits small size satellites (up to 250-280 kg). GONETS satellites are not equipped with a correction subsystem. Therefore the task is to improve the efficiency of the space communication system to correct the orbit parameters without satellite modification, increasing the number of satellites in the orbital group and without changing the type of launch vehicle used. To tackle this task the specialists and engineers of NPO PM carried out investigations into the influence of the compensation accuracy of the initial injection errors and the orbit keeping accuracy on the time probability response (any time during which the communication session will probably take place). They designed a simulation model to carry out their investigations.

articleTitle: Project SIBNET
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The telecommunication project SIBNET for Siberia is discussed. Specialists believe that the project will allow affective computer communication in the USA-Russia-China region through the American satellite communication system INTELSAT. The main executors of the project are the American company Datron Telecommunications International Inc., the firm "Horizon" from Shushenskoe, and the Tomsk firm "Tomteleport". Several Siberian enterprises have announced the creation of a joint enterprise. These enterprises will organize the system of satellite communication in Siberia.

articleTitle: Direct TV broadcasting system based on GALS and GALS-R satellites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The creation of a multiprogramme TV broadcasting system in Russia is of great significance for the political, economical and cultural life of the country. The territory of Russia is covered by two TV programmes. Increasing the number of programmes to 5...6 is discussed. The only possible solution to this problem may be the accelerated development of a satellite direct TV broadcasting systems (DBS). To fulfil this target the DBS GALS family is being created. The authors show the major technical performance and service areas over Russian territory of the GALS and Gals-R spacecraft. The applications of these spacecraft will allow one to receive DBS programmes using individual sets with antenna diameters of about 0.6-1.0 m. Head earth stations operating with cable networks will be used to organize the major channels to supply TV centres with TV programmes.

articleTitle: On-board signal processing in spread spectrum low orbit systems by acoustoelectronic devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: One of the main problem of low orbiting satellite multiple access repeater design is creating of small mass-size and low power consumption equipment to process the group signal. The next problem of that satellite communication system development is ensuring the electromagnetic compatibility. The application of direct spread frequency spectrum (DS-SS) signals and acoustoelectronics (AE) devices is one solution to these problems. The construction of the acoustoelectronic group signal processing device for the hybrid code and time channel division multiple access to the orbiting satellite repeater is discussed. The combined coherent-noncoherent direct sequence spread spectrum signal processing capability is demonstrated for a mobile communication network with high frequency instability of the receiving signals. The signal energy losses on account of the DS-SS signal processing by the acoustoelectronic convolver and the noncoherent integrator is analysed. The recommendations for the energy loss reduction and the resulting increase in the number of users are formulated. The network characteristics of the low orbit satellite with an acoustoelectronic processing device are estimated.

articleTitle: Mobile satellite system with LEO-HEO switched interlink
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Describes the design of a two-level satellite configuration: one high-Earth-orbit (HEO) satellite linked with many LEO satellites to supply reliable communication for a moving satellite terminal in the low reliability region bounds of the HEO-satellite.

articleTitle: TME JOINT STOCK COMPANY TELECOM AND RESPECTIVES OF BUSINESS COOPERATION
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94

articleTitle: Architecture of a modeling program complex for satellite data network with dynamically variable topology investigation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Discusses networks of information transfer based on moving objects. The main characteristics of such networks-dynamically changing characteristics of the band channels, topology, etc.-make it impossible to use plain analytical methods of analysis of such systems. The author discusses the SATNET modelling program for this analysis.

articleTitle: On construction of global satellite multiprogram global information system using "storm" warning signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The setting-up of multipurpose circular communication by adding extra digital signals to TV program signals is the real way to increase efficiency of the existing TV transmission network. These additional signals can be graphic and facsimile information and can be received in every point within TV broadcasting coverage areas in this country and abroad by ordinary TV sets or simplified receivers. Data transmission through such TV channels make it possible not only to save expensive and deficient telephone channels, but also to speed up data provision for remote and inaccessible regions. Tests of this new and original system (teleinform), developed by the Radio Research Institute of the RF Ministry of Communications, proved its advantages while transmitting information to places where Russian TV programs are available. An interesting project entitled SAPS (Solar Activity Patrol System), developed by the Space Research Institute of The RF Academy of Sciences, can play an exceptionally important role in the implementation of the Solar Ecological Security Programme. The solar storm warning signals, generated by SAPS and included in the above described information system, besides its main humanitarian and economic function substantially improve commercial characteristics of the system. The distribution system of this information throughout the world may be organized in the most cost-effective way by using the existing terrestrial and satellite channels.

articleTitle: Fail-safe gyromoment attitude control systems of communication, navigation, and land-survey satellites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Presents new results for the creation of fault-tolerant gyromoment attitude control systems (ACSs) for multipurpose and specialized spacecraft for communication, navigation and land-surveying, application of mathematical methods, and algorithms, and software for dynamics investigations.

articleTitle: INTERSPUTNIK's role in Eastern Europe
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: INTERSPUTNIK is an independent international intergovernmental organization which commercially operates a satellite communications system. INTERSPUTNIK has an indepth knowledge of both the existing condition of telecommunications sector in each country and the requirements for the development of the region's telecommunications services. The current Russian-made "Gorizont" satellites are to be replaced with the more advanced Russian "Express" series. Each new satellite will have at least fifty C- and Ku-band transponders with the antenna patterns of the different configurations having special shapes. The basic transponder specifications of the new satellite are shown. INTERSPUTNIK has been considering the possibility of assisting the former Soviet republics in developing both international and domestic telecommunications.

articleTitle: The perspective of satellite television development in Russia
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The concept of satellite TV and radio broadcasting development in Russia is being currently worked out by the Russian Federal Television and Radio Service. The work is being carried out with allowance made for the state budget and market economy mechanism. It is vital for the Russian Satellite Television System to be based, mainly, on local budgets and regional market structures. The plans made for the development of this system are to cover special needs of the country regions and their economic possibilities which have strong dependability of both the density of population and the production development level in a particular region. The authors come to the conclusion that the satellite "Gals" is an ideal option to serve European Russia and satellite "Express" is good enough to supply services for Asian Russia.

articleTitle: Research of limit probability-time characteristic of reliability of satellite connection networks with dynamically variable topology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The present work examines the problems of the limiting probability-time characteristics of reliability of satellite connection systems with dynamically variable topology. The analytical methods of calculation of structure reliability and stability are examined, and a comparison with some probable satellite connection systems structure is made.

articleTitle: "Informsviaz"; large-scale integrated services communication network (ISCN). ISCN bank being taken as an example
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: An integrated services communication system based on backbone satellite channels with a developed terrestrial part is described. The system is to provide banks which have a large number of branches, situated in different republics of CIS as well as abroad, with a reliable and cost-effective means of communication. The system also illustrates the general approach of Informsviaz to development of corporate wide area communication systems. The system described has three levels of nodes which corresponds to structure of the bank and to information flow within the bank. The software system developed by Informsviaz and aimed to link earth stations in one network gives an opportunity for large numbers of users to share a limited number of channels. Customers are also free to choose earth stations and satellite modems from a wide range of equipment produced in CIS or abroad. The system is one of the first Russian produced systems with shared (switched) satellite channels (not fixed ones) which have been put into operation. The first version of the system was implemented in 1993 for the "Vostok" Bank, which has about 30 branches all around CIS and abroad. Different modifications of the general purpose control system of the satellite communication network are described. The versions can serve for the purposes of data and voice transfer. Data can be transferred in interactive or in store and forward mode. Data access can be performed via the X.25 interface. A description of the network node structure is given.

articleTitle: New technology of the airborne system satellite control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Summary form only given. Data on the technology developed to fabricate electron systems for satellite control based on hybrid integrated functional devices on polyimide film multilayer patch boards and packageless integrated microcircuits on polyimide substrates is given in this report. Existing results about the high reliability of the space airborne equipment, fabricated in this manner are given. The typical base design, realizing the principal advantages of the above technology are described.

articleTitle: SovCan STAR satellite communications system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The SovCan STAR satellite communications system will provide a variety of services by establishing of domestic and international communications networks. These networks will provide fixed multipurpose communications services. The SovCan STAR networks will be compatible with existing networks and can be used by subscribers equipped with the small ground stations. The SovCan STAR satellite communications system consists of five satellites operating in a geosynchronous orbit. These satellites will be located in the orbital slots between 14/spl deg/ West and 145/spl deg/ East. The SovCan STAR payload consists of 24 Ku-band (14/11 GHz) transponders each with a useable bandwidth of 54 MHz connected to four steerable antennas with a combined transmit and receive capability. Each antenna can receive or transmit up to 8 channels.

articleTitle: Integrated multipurpose multilevel space communication system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: At the present time many space systems (SS) of different purpose operate and are being designed. As independently developed directions, the research orbital stations (manned and automatic), space telemetry and telecontrol, satellite communications, observation and remote sensing from space, space navigation, have seen the most expansion. Many SS use or will use an allocated telecommunications network, its channel, switching, program-operational resources, to give information to the end user, subscriber. In its turn, this network has trends to use widely analog SS resources. These facts are one of the principal motives for integrating many services of the switching support for the different purpose spacecrafts.

articleTitle: System of official distribution of digital information with use of the second transponder of direct television broadcast satellite
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The second transponder intended for television broadcasting for the 1 dB wave range in the Siberia region is not being exploited properly due to high levels of interference. Thus, the potential capabilities of the "Ekran-M" satellite are not being used completely. It is suggested that the digital data transmission satellite system "Ekran-D" should be organized in order to increase the efficiency of exploiting the "Ekran-M" satellite.

articleTitle: Space systems for the exploration of the land and ocean natural resources and proposal for their development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Firstly, Earth observation space systems which are in operation during the period 1994-1997 are discussed. Then proposals on the development of an operative Earth observation system for the period 1997-2005 are outlined, including structure of the Earth remote sensing system, 'Planeta-O'.

articleTitle: Satellite communication system active phased arrays (APA)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: A series of active phased arrays (APA) is considered, which are intended for use in various systems. The given information indicates the possible uses of APA. The first group includes APA designed for the UHF band. These APA were developed for a satellite communication system which could work with the "MOLNIYA" relay high elliptical orbit. The system is suitable for transportable, aeroplane, automobile, ship, and subscriber station communications. The second APA group considered includes satellite transponders, and transmitting and receiving APA for different frequency bands.

articleTitle: Radioholographic antenna for ionospheric retranslation in broadcasting and communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The concept of passive or active retranslation of RF signals by means of a radioholographic antenna (RHA) is presented. The chosen domain of the atmosphere (at 30-70 km altitude) is illuminated from the Earth by a powerful microwave electromagnetic field. This field has special spectrum and space distributions, providing in the volume near to the selected point in atmosphere the following factors: (1) artificial ionized plasma generation; 2) stabilization of the generated plasma by the way of its organization into the most energetically stable form (plasmoid) by means of the plasma-supplying series of microwave impulses; (3) projection of the radioholographic image onto the plasmoid, so that the last be able to receive RF signals, coming from the preset direction and retransmit them to the prescribed direction. During the useful signals retransmission, the separation of some part of the RHA power is possible, i.e. the parametric amplification of the retranslated signals may take place.

articleTitle: Analysis of low orbit satellite communications systems alternate design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: This report is a comparative analysis of satellite communications systems main design variants taking into account economical and temporal characteristics. The estimations used are qualitative and are derived from the simplified image of the system and its users.

articleTitle: "TSIKADA-M-UTTH" multi-purposes satellite system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The TSK multi-purpose satellite system has been developed to replace first generation low-orbit navigation systems as well as the COSPAS-SARSAT system. The system will provide operations for both existing customers and new customers having advanced equipment. TSK is to perform the following tasks: definition of the location of an unlimited number of mobile customers in any region of the globe independently of weather; maritime vehicles and aeroplanes location definition in an emergency; support the ELECON-STIR system: consignment monitoring and traffic control. The orbital constellation consists of seven satellites which are located within seven orbital planes equally distributed along the equator in longitude (circular orbit height is about 1,000 km; orbit inclination is 83 ang. degrees). This provides for customers to be in touch with the satellite on average for 90 minutes in equatorial regions, 45 minutes at mid-latitudes, and 20 minutes at high geographical latitudes.

articleTitle: C-band power amplifier MIC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: A 5.9 to 6.45 GHz MIC amplifier module has been developed for use in satellite transponders. The amplifier module demonstrated an output power from 120 to 3000 mW. The key elements of all the C-band MIC are domestic GaAs FETs.

articleTitle: The communication satellite "Yamal": the new technological approach in creating the communication satellites in Russia
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: The new satellite communication system "Yamal" based on geostationary satellites is created by the joint-stock company GAZCOM for the gas industry and other customers. The communication satellite "Yamal" is the main element of the system space segment. The "Yamal" system includes two standard communication satellites: the western satellite in a 19.5/spl deg/W orbital position and the eastern satellite in a 75/spl deg/E orbital position. The paper present the main characteristics of the standard communication satellite of the "Yamal" system.

publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Satellite Communications. ICSC'94
abstract: Presents the front cover of the proceedings record.
